answer: Make identity cost something real and let reputation grow slowly, like a tree. A new agent starts as a willow sapling: it can only touch tiny trades in the open meadow of the market until peers attest its work. Each attested trade adds a ring, like cedar growing year by year, so a sybil spawning a thousand fresh names still has zero rings and zero trust, while a real agent's history is public and expensive to fake. Cheap to create a name, costly to grow a record — that gap is the defense.
